name: health
documentation: HTTP liveness and readiness probes for the dependencies of the running process. GET /health is liveness and touches nothing external; GET /health/ready checks every bound port and answers 503 when one is down; GET /health/{probe} reports one. Does NOT answer whether the machine can run the kernel — that is `hkm doctor`, which stays the single authority on environment problems.
//liveness: Point a container's LIVENESS probe at /health and its READINESS probe at /health/ready. The distinction is load-bearing: a failed liveness probe RESTARTS the container while a failed readiness probe only removes it from the load balancer, so a liveness probe that touches the database makes an orchestrator kill every replica during a database blip — adding a restart storm to an outage that a restart cannot fix.
//static-beats-dynamic: /ready is declared alongside /{probe:alpha} on purpose. The kernel resolves static routes before dynamic ones, so /health/ready reaches ready() and never the one-probe handler.
//no-filters: This module declares no routeFilters. A health endpoint behind the application's own auth or throttle stages stops answering for exactly the reasons it exists to report. Detail is gated by HEALTH_TOKEN inside the controller instead, so the probe itself always answers.
